newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ranged at central bank's top level.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ranged at central bank's top level.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was stuck in a tight range on Tuesday morning as the dollar-rupee exchange rate was close to the Central Bank's selling level, dealers said.
At 0530 GMT, the rupee was at 59.37 to the dollar after opening at 59.35. On Monday the rupee closed at 59.39 against the U.S. unit.
"Upto now there seems to be only commercial demand, which is being covered with dollars from the Central Bank," said an American Express Bank dealer.
"Speculators are absent due to the exchange rate already being near the Central Bank's top," he said.
The Central Bank, responding to the greenback's lack of movement overseas, kept its rate unchanged at 58.1947 and 59.3703.

"Many speculators must have accumulated positions because people have been buying for the past few days," a Commercial Bank dealer said. "In one or two days, if rates move up, they may start selling."
Overnight call money rate, which opened at 9.5 percent, fell to 9.25 percent after a number of big lenders entered the market, dealers said.
